briefs.claim_en: COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips to track vaccinated individuals.
briefs.brief_en: Multiple health authorities and fact-checking organizations have debunked the claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips. The CDC and Mayo Clinic state that vaccines do not contain microchips and are designed to stimulate the immune system. Pfizer's official website also confirms the absence of microchips. The Indonesian Ministry of Health on May 28, 2021, and the Indonesian Ministry of Communication and Information have also refuted these claims, clarifying that barcodes on vaccine products are for distribution tracking, not individual tracking. Fact-checkers like AFP (July 14, 2021) and FactCheck.org (May 26, 2022) have addressed various iterations of this conspiracy theory, including misinterpretations of microrobots and health sensors, and spoof videos.
